q: What is the single module load command on Aurora that brings in IPEX-enabled PyTorch and TensorFlow?
gold: module load frameworks

q: What is the production PBS queue name on Aurora?
gold: prod (the production queue is named 'prod' on Aurora)

q: What is the absolute mount path of Aurora's project Lustre filesystem?
gold: /lus/flare (project directories live under /lus/flare/projects/<project>/)

q: Which MPI launcher binary is used to start MPI ranks on Aurora compute nodes?
gold: mpiexec (Aurora uses mpiexec from MPICH/PALS — NOT srun, NOT aprun)

q: What is the official name of the GPU model in each Aurora compute node?
gold: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 (also known as Ponte Vecchio / PVC). Each node has 6 GPUs / 12 tiles.

q: How many PVC GPU tiles are exposed per Aurora compute node?
gold: 12 tiles per node (6 GPUs × 2 tiles each)

q: Which PyTorch device string targets the Intel GPU on Aurora?
gold: 'xpu' (e.g. tensor.to('xpu') or torch.device('xpu')). Requires `import intel_extension_for_pytorch` first.

q: What is the Intel oneAPI compiler driver name for compiling SYCL C++ code on Aurora?
gold: icpx (with the -fsycl flag). The legacy 'dpcpp' driver is deprecated.

q: What command-line debugger ships with oneAPI for stepping through SYCL kernels on a PVC GPU?
gold: gdb-oneapi (Intel's GDB extension that supports SYCL/OpenCL/Level-Zero device-code debugging).

q: Which container runtime is supported on Aurora compute nodes?
gold: Apptainer (formerly Singularity). Load via `module load apptainer`. Docker is not supported.

q: Write a minimal PBS script header (just the #PBS lines) requesting 4 nodes for 60 minutes on the prod queue, charging project gpu_hack, with home and flare filesystems mounted, and merging stderr into stdout.
gold:
#!/bin/bash -l
#PBS -A gpu_hack
#PBS -q prod
#PBS -l select=4
#PBS -l walltime=01:00:00
#PBS -l filesystems=home:flare
#PBS -j oe

q: Show the full mpiexec command to run 96 MPI ranks across 8 Aurora nodes with one rank per PVC tile (12 ranks/node), each rank pinned to a distinct tile.
gold: mpiexec -n 96 -ppn 12 gpu_tile_compact.sh ./my_app — `gpu_tile_compact.sh` sets ZE_AFFINITY_MASK so each of the 12 ranks per node lands on a distinct PVC tile.

q: Set the ZE_AFFINITY_MASK environment variable so a single process sees only tile 0 of GPU 1.
gold: export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=1.0  (format is <device-id>.<sub-device-id>; tile 0 of GPU 1 = '1.0').

q: What backend should torch.distributed.init_process_group use on Aurora for multi-tile collective communication, and what import is needed first?
gold: Use backend='ccl' (Intel oneCCL). Must `import oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch` before init_process_group to register it. NCCL is CUDA-only.

q: What launcher pattern serves a model with vLLM across all 12 PVC tiles of a single Aurora node?
gold: mpiexec -n 12 -ppn 12 gpu_tile_compact.sh vllm serve <model> --tensor-parallel-size 12. The wrapper binds each rank to one tile; --tensor-parallel-size 12 shards the model.

q: Show the icpx command to ahead-of-time (AOT) compile a SYCL source file kernel.cpp specifically for Aurora's PVC GPUs.
gold: icpx -fsycl -fsycl-targets=spir64_gen -Xs '-device pvc' kernel.cpp -o kernel

q: Give the one-line VTune command to collect a GPU hotspots profile of ./my_app on Aurora.
gold: vtune -collect gpu-hotspots -result-dir vtune_gpu ./my_app  (then summarize with `vtune -report summary -result-dir vtune_gpu` or open vtune-gui).

q: Show the commands to (a) create a POSIX container in DAOS pool `mypool`, (b) mount it at /tmp/dfuse_mnt on a compute node.
gold:
(a) daos cont create mypool --type POSIX  (returns a UUID/label)
(b) dfuse --pool mypool --container <cont> --mountpoint /tmp/dfuse_mnt
(unmount with `fusermount3 -u /tmp/dfuse_mnt`)

q: Recommend a single `lfs setstripe` command for a directory that will hold multi-GB checkpoint files on /lus/flare.
gold: lfs setstripe -c 48 -S 16M <dir>  (48 OST stripe count, 16 MiB stripe size — recommended high-bandwidth setting for large files on flare)

q: I have CUDA training code that does `model.to('cuda:0')` and `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`. What is the minimal patch to make it run on Aurora's PVC?
gold: Add `import intel_extension_for_pytorch` at the top, replace 'cuda:0' with 'xpu:0' (or 'xpu'), and replace `torch.cuda.empty_cache()` with `torch.xpu.empty_cache()`. For distributed, swap NCCL for CCL via oneccl_bindings_for_pytorch and backend='ccl'.

q: When linking a multi-file SYCL application with icpx, do you need `-fsycl` only at compile time, only at link time, or both? Why?
gold: Both. `-fsycl` at compile time enables the SYCL frontend; at link time it pulls in the SYCL runtime libraries and triggers the device-code packaging (sycl-post-link). Omitting it from the link step produces 'undefined reference' errors against the SYCL runtime symbols.

q: I'm porting a Cray job script that calls `aprun -n 192 -N 24 ./solver`. What is the equivalent on Aurora and why?
gold: Equivalent: mpiexec -n 192 -ppn 24 ./solver (optionally with gpu_tile_compact.sh for tile binding). Aurora uses MPICH/PALS mpiexec — NOT Cray ALPS aprun. The flag rename: -N → -ppn, -n stays the same.

q: Why is it dangerous to `pip install torch` into the venv after `module load frameworks` on Aurora, and what's the symptom if you do?
gold: Frameworks ships an Aurora-tuned torch (2.10.x) tightly coupled to IPEX, torchvision, and the oneAPI SYCL runtime. `pip install torch` pulls a generic CPU/CUDA wheel (e.g. torch 2.6.0+cpu), which gets prepended in the venv's site-packages and overrides the frameworks one. Symptoms: ImportError on torchvision::nms (operator missing because the new torch + frameworks-built torchvision are mismatched), XPU disappears, training crashes at import. Fix: pip uninstall torch (and torchao/torchvision if also clobbered) to restore the frameworks build.

q: Why might starting a PBS script with `set -u` cause it to die silently right after `source env.sh` (which runs `module load`), and how do you fix it?
gold: Lmod's `module` shell function references some unbound shell variables internally during a load. With `set -u` (nounset) active, the first such reference triggers an unbound-variable error and the shell exits before any of your script's commands run — leaving zero output (the redirected stdout file is empty). Fix: don't use `set -u` in PBS scripts that source env.sh, OR temporarily `set +u` around the `source ... env.sh` and re-enable after.

q: If I write `#PBS -o phase1_${PBS_JOBID}.out`, does PBS substitute the job ID into the filename? Why or why not, and what's the recommended pattern?
gold: No — PBS does NOT substitute shell variables in #PBS directives. The directive is parsed before the shell starts, so the literal string `phase1_${PBS_JOBID}.out` is taken verbatim as the filename. Recommended patterns: (1) use a directory-only -o (e.g. `#PBS -o /path/to/logs/`) and let PBS append `<jobname>.o<jobid>`, or (2) omit -o entirely so PBS uses default `<jobname>.o<jobid>` in the submission directory.

q: What environment variable enables GPU-aware MPI on Aurora's MPICH so that you can pass an XPU device pointer directly to MPI_Send/Recv?
gold: MPICH_GPU_SUPPORT_ENABLED=1 (must be set before mpiexec). With this, MPICH recognizes Level Zero / SYCL device pointers in MPI_Send/Recv and uses GPU-IPC or RDMA paths instead of staging through the host.

q: I want to fine-tune a 70B Llama with LoRA on a single Aurora node (12 PVC tiles). What's the difference between using HF `device_map='auto'` (naive model parallel) vs setting up DDP + ZeRO across all 12 tiles, and which would I pick for this size?
gold: device_map='auto' is naive layer-by-layer pipeline (model parallel): one tile at a time runs forward/backward, others sit idle. Throughput is roughly 1/12 of one tile (no pipelining) — very slow but trivial to set up. DDP+ZeRO replicates layers across tiles and shards optimizer states (ZeRO-2/3) so all 12 tiles compute in parallel, reducing per-step time ~10-12x with comm overhead. For 70B + LoRA on 1 node, DDP+ZeRO-3 is the right choice — model_parallel via device_map only makes sense as a quick smoke test or when the model can't fit on a single tile and you don't have time to set up distributed training.

q: I'm hitting Sophia's gpt-oss-120b inference endpoint from 20 ranks × 4 worker threads each (80 concurrent HTTPS requests). I'm seeing ~10% of requests fail with HTTP 429 / 503. What's the cause and a fix that doesn't reduce my total request count?
gold: The Sophia gpt-oss-120b service is rate-limited around ~50 concurrent requests; 80 simultaneous in-flight requests overwhelm it, returning 429 (Too Many Requests) or 503 (Service Unavailable). Two fixes that preserve total throughput: (1) reduce concurrency to ~40 (e.g. workers=2 per rank instead of 4), and (2) stagger rank startup with `sleep $((RANK*30))` so the 20 ranks don't all hit the endpoint in the same second. Combined: 20 ranks × 2 workers = 40 concurrent, ramped over 10 min. Also implement HTTP retry-with-backoff on 429/503.

q: I'm training Gemma-3 (270M) with LoRA on a PVC tile via HuggingFace + IPEX, attn_implementation='sdpa', and it crashes with 'Segmentation fault from GPU at ... type: 0 (NotPresent), level: 1 (PDE), access: 1 (Write)' partway through training. What's the cause and how do you work around it?
gold: PVC's SDPA backend on PyTorch 2.10 / IPEX has a bug broadcasting Gemma-3's grouped-query attention (Q has more heads than K/V), triggering a GPU page fault on certain batch shapes. Workaround: pass `attn_implementation='eager'` instead of 'sdpa' when loading the model. Eager attention is slower but bypasses the SDPA broadcasting bug. (For very long sequences in C3-style splits, the bug can also recur with eager — drop max_seq_length or filter out the longest examples.)

q: I installed Unsloth's `intel-gpu-torch290` extras into a separate venv. When I try to import torch I get 'libsycl.so.8: undefined symbol: urEnqueueCooperativeKernelLaunchExp, version LIBUR_LOADER_0.12'. What's the root cause and what would have to change to make Unsloth work on this Aurora system today?
gold: Unsloth's bundled libsycl.so.8 (from a 2026.x oneAPI snapshot) calls `urEnqueueCooperativeKernelLaunchExp`, a Unified Runtime experimental API present in newer UR loader builds but NOT in the libur_loader.so.0.12.0 shipped with Aurora's installed oneAPI (compiler/2025.3). The symbol versioning advertises LIBUR_LOADER_0.12 in both, but the symbol set is a strict superset on Unsloth's side. Workarounds require getting a newer system UR loader (Aurora-side oneAPI upgrade — out of user control) or rebuilding Unsloth's torch-2.9.0+xpu wheel against Aurora's exact toolchain (multi-day effort). Practical conclusion: Unsloth is not usable on Aurora today; stick with the frameworks-shipped torch 2.10 + IPEX path for XPU training.
